points.description: States that the statement is FALSE.

Justifies FALSE: each process is an independent entity that needs its own separate OS state or PCB (tracking its own execution, memory contents, open files, memory allocations and stack), so a PCB cannot be shared among processes of the same program.
points.partial_credit: Half marks (0.75) if the student says each process needs separate state or its own PCB but gives no reason, or only lists some of the per-process state items.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) need the answer FALSE together with a justification that each process is independent and needs its own PCB or separate OS state (execution state, memory, open files, stack), so one shared PCB cannot serve several processes. Per the exam rule, a correct FALSE with no correct justification earns no marks, so the justification carries most of the weight. A justification that gives the separate-state idea but is vague or misses the per-process detail earns half of P2. An answer of TRUE, or a justification that describes shared PCBs or reference counting as correct, earns no marks.
